program: Uninsured adult primary, dental, behavioral and navigation care in McHenry County

what: Family Health Partnership Clinic provides primary, dental and behavioral care to uninsured adults in McHenry County.
Its onsite dispensary and referral coordination can make treatment and chronic-disease management more accessible.
The narrow conditional reference is $30.969 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents; it is not a calibrated estimate of the whole clinic or a marginal donation.
strengths: Local continuity of care, medication dispensing and coordinated referrals address practical access barriers.
The current report separates visits, therapy and prescriptions from health outcomes; cohort deduplication still needs verification.
The original audit now reconciles full recognized resources, including thrift inventory and donated services.
reservations: No local causal utility, event reduction, household savings or donor-expansion response was verified.
Hypertension control is not a symptom improvement, and diabetes and hypertension cohorts can overlap.
Unrecognized volunteer opportunity costs, other program outcomes and the government-funding claim need further reconciliation.

sections.what: Family Health Partnership Clinic, EIN 36-4277029, is the Crystal Lake recipient serving uninsured McHenry County adults within the Chicago metro. It provides medical, dental, pharmacy and behavioral care, with specialty referrals when available. Its official site links the existing Network for Good giving route; an actual checkout was not verified. Patients face sliding fees but are not turned away for inability to pay. Medicaid, Medicare and private insurance are not accepted.
sections.monitoring: FY2025 reports 6,093 visits, 321 new-patient visits, 626 therapy sessions, 12,437 prescriptions and 509 medical/dental volunteer hours. These are outputs, not unique annual people or additional health. January–June graphs visibly report 67% diabetes and 84% hypertension control. Comparator case mix differs, so these do not establish causal improvement. Text extraction from the original PDF third page contains '245 Patients' and '409 Patients', but these counts are NOT visible in the rendered page. They may be obsolete or hidden design text and are not verified observed cohorts. N=409 is therefore retained only as an unsupported narrow chronic-care population hypothesis, not a source-established count. The 245 sensitivity is another hypothetical cohort, not measured diabetes exposure. Unique patients, dose, households and condition overlap remain unknown. Other clinical, dental, therapy and navigation benefits and burdens remain unknown, not zero; the annual denominator is broader than the priced channel.
sections.qualitative: Hypertension is often asymptomatic; good control mainly prevents future cardiovascular events, rather than automatically delivering .05 immediate utility. The retained .30 additional response, .05 utility and half-year duration are weak explicit reference priors, not calibrated local evidence. No control percentage is used as a response rate. A separate finite cardiovascular hypothesis replaces, rather than adds to, the short morbidity area. SPRINT randomized intensive versus standard blood-pressure targets among older high-risk adults without diabetes or stroke. Its initial annual composite event rates were 1.65% versus 2.19%, but serious hypotension, syncope, electrolyte abnormalities and kidney events were higher with intensive therapy. The clinic is not that intervention or population. Event sensitivity uses the observed .0054 annual difference, a judged .25 transfer, three finite years and an unsupported one-equivalent loss per composite event; no separately recurring mortality or survivor earnings are credited. An additional harm stress covers the whole exposed cohort. This illustrates uncertainty, not a recommended local efficacy estimate.
sections.cost:
The original FY2025 audit reports $2,538,482 expenses. It already includes $54,077 direct donor benefits and recognized professional services, so neither is added again. Pink Door sales separately net $100,874 inventory cost, producing full gross recognized resources of $2,639,356. The 990 reconciliation reaches the same audit amount through $2,393,158 functional expenses + $86,349 donated services + $58,975 event expense. The different audit event classification is not an extra cost. Note 9 recognizes $73,999 professional services and $12,350 other services; unpaid volunteer time is not reflected. The central recognized-resource boundary therefore does not establish complete economic cost. $25,000/$100,000 additional nonoverlapping volunteer opportunity budgets and unknown-cost cases are separate. Current official financial links yielded FY2025 only; comparable prior full-cost years were not verified in this bounded review.

Full annual costs remain in the denominator. b=.35 is an unsupported annual funded-work response beyond replacement funding, alternative care and volunteer capacity, not an extra haircut on already demonstrated incremental outcomes. b=1 is shown. A marginal gift has no verified capacity price. The judged 409-person narrow cohort × .35 exposes 143.15 patient units; .30 clinical response gives 42.945 people. Half-year .05 utility, quarter-year delay, 3% discount and .98 metro share give 1.044406 clinical QALYs. The old 6,093 × .25 episode prior and $6.735524 million health-only price are frozen diagnostically; narrowing is a scope correction, not proof that all other benefits are absent.

Signed household resources are counted separately and once. A .30 resource-success prior among the same exposure means 42.945 households avoid $300 actually otherwise-paid medical spending within one year, net of alternative insurance/charity, forgone care, taxes, benefits and replacement. This is not retail service value or face-value debt, and these households are not assumed identical to clinical responders. Work gain is unknown-neutral at $0, not measured zero. Each positive component retains .5 for health overlap; each negative remains full. All exposed patients incur a judged $100 incremental annual total for repeated-visit travel, missed work, copays and added care versus alternatives, including unsuccessful or clinically untreated patients. Success households net $50; 100.205 others lose $100. One patient per household and one welfare-equivalent person per household are reference judgments, not observed family size. A two-patients-per-household case aggregates both patients' costs before one log; it does not count visits as households. Baseline annual household resources are judged $20,000. .5 × people × discounted years × log(1 + net/baseline) gives −.192151 resource equivalents and .852255 combined equivalents, implying $30.969081 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

Clinical-null preserves all resource exposure and burdens. Financial-only, adverse, true-zero, no savings, no expansion and complete unknown are distinct. Clinical people are a subset of resource exposure; harms cover the full union. Provider/payer net-margin loss and additional own-resource cost stresses are distinct household incidence, excluding clinical input costs already in the denominator. Central external incidence is unknown-neutral and may include positive or negative offsets; the headline is a partial boundary, not complete world net benefit. Ordinary survivor wages, prescription retail prices, food pounds and thrift retail multipliers are not income benefits.
sections.funding: The audit records $1,387,765 grants, $336,676 program fees, $5,575,072 net assets and $3,758,041 financial assets available within twelve months; the 990 classifies $1,387,765 government grants. The annual report's no-government-reliance wording does not reconcile with whole-entity government receipts. The official program page separately identifies county Mental Health Board navigation funding, but this does not prove it explains all receipts. Ask for the clinical/navigation funding split and whether restricted funding can expand the priced cohort. Note 8 describes $4,210,376 held by a community foundation with redirection power, excluded from the clinic balance sheet, not immediately available clinic cash. Reserves do not prove zero useful expansion. Sliding-fee/FQHC care, hospital charity, changing insurance eligibility and forgone treatment are relevant alternatives; no same retail treatment purchase is assumed. No priced unfunded volunteer capacity or next-gift treatment commitment was verified.

model.costScope: Full annual recognized recipient resources across clinic, navigation and thrift; unrecognized volunteers and complete economic cost unknown.
model.geographicAttribution: McHenry County Chicago metro; .98 residence prior; source geography not measured beneficiary residence.
model.formula: Health=N*b*treatedFraction*a*u*discountedYears(T)−N*b*harm, then local share. Alternate event health replaces utility with .0054*eventTransfer*eventQ*discountedYears(3). Income=.5*HH*discountedYears(1)*log1p(joint signed net/HH baseline); positives overlap individually, negatives/costs full. Headline=10*(C+volunteerBudget)/(clinical+income).
model.counterfactual: Existing sliding-fee/FQHC, hospital charity, insurance eligibility, substitute funding and forgone care; no retail-price assumption.
model.attribution: No causal increment demonstrated. Annual response .35 is a conditional reference, not measured donor elasticity.
model.uncertainty: Whole portfolio, unrecognized resource cost and marginal gift remain unknown. Central is an unsupported narrow reference, not calibrated EV or lower bound.
model.nativeOutcomes: Visible visits, sessions, prescriptions and tests are outputs, not incremental outcomes. Control percentages are noncausal. Hidden PDF text contains 245/409 patient labels not visible in the rendered original, so neither is a verified cohort. N=409 is an unsupported population hypothesis.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Full filed expense plus netted events/inventory and donated services from original Schedule D; external-care sensitivity adds assumed $1m, not an observed estimate.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: a removes equivalent care elsewhere and ineffective care; b separately removes replacement financing/volunteer capacity. One morbidity pathway avoids double counting.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: McHenry uninsured adult mission; .98 allows unmeasured mobility/residency leakage; excludes Kenosha and other non-MSA counties.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Central illustrative scenario and favorable/poor bounds are judgments, not calibrated EV or confidence interval. Cross-recipient results cannot be summed without deduplication. These costs are whole-portfolio equivalents, not marginal gift purchase guarantees. Cost numerators use different accounting recognition of donated care; central prices must not be interpreted as a comparable economic-efficiency ranking. Favorable and poor scenarios are illustrative cases, not exhaustive bounds.
